content: Articulin F (articulin) is prescribed with indication-specific dosing, detailed adverse effect profiles based on frequency, comprehensive drug interaction data, contraindications, pregnancy and lactation guidelines, and cost information. The recommended dosage is two capsules taken orally three times daily (450 mg total). Each capsule contains the following active ingredients: 100 mg of Withania somnifera (commonly known as withania or ashwagandha), 50 mg of Boswellia serrata (also referred to as boswellia or Indian frankincense), 50 mg of Curcuma longa (commonly known as turmeric), and a zinc complex. This formulation is primarily indicated for the management of osteoarthritis. Clinical studies have demonstrated a significant reduction in pain and disability scores in patients using this medication, although no radiographic changes in joint structure were observed. Reported adverse effects include nausea, abdominal pain, dermatitis, and hypersensitivity reactions. Regarding pregnancy, the medication is categorized as N/A, but it is generally considered acceptable for use. Controlled studies conducted in pregnant women have not shown evidence of fetal risk. Information on lactation safety is also categorized as N/A.
